reference_summary: Feeder 7 relay setting group S3 had an instantaneous pickup of 1,200 A, intended for normal load. The cold-load pickup current for the feeder was calculated to reach 1,950 A rms for twelve cycles. At 09:12:33.54, breaker 52-1 closed to restore power to Synthetic Feeder 7. Feeder 7 supplied 87 induction motors and one triac-switched capacitor bank at a pre-outage load of 41 MW. The relay's 50 instantaneous element tripped at 09:12:33.72 when the measured current exceeded the 1,200 A setting. Breaker 52-1 opened at 09:12:33.80, interrupting the feeder current with a 32 ms opening time. Synthetic Feeder 7 remained de-energized for 43 minutes until an operator remotely switched the setting group. The 29.4 MWh energy loss was calculated as 41 MW times the 43 minute outage duration. An engineer changed relay setting group to S4 at 09:55, raising instantaneous pickup to 2,000 A. The operator manually closed breaker 52-1 at 09:56, and the feeder successfully picked up cold load.
title: Incorrect Instantaneous Overcurrent Setting Causes Feeder 7 Lockout During Cold Load Restoration

reference_summary: Substation relay 51N on feeder 12 had a time-overcurrent pickup of 1,200 A with a 0.6 s time dial. Recloser R-2's time dial was erroneously set to 2.0 after the controller replacement. At 10:27:15, breaker 52-2 at Synthetic Substation B closed to energize Synthetic Feeder 12. A tree squirrel touched phase B terminal on a downstream transformer, initiating a solid ground fault. At 10:27:19.01, the 51N ground relay tripped breaker 52-2 after a 0.65 s delay. Breaker 52-2 opened in 3 cycles, isolating the entire feeder from the source. Synthetic Feeder 12 remained de-energized for one hour twenty minutes, causing a load loss of 13.5 MW. The unsupplied energy was 18 MWh, equal to 13.5 MW times 80 minutes. At 11:45, an engineer remotely changed recloser R-2's setting group to group 2, restoring a 0.5 s time dial. Operators closed breaker 52-2 at 11:47, after confirming the feeder was in a normal no-fault condition.
title: Ground Fault Relay Miscoordination Lockout on Synthetic Feeder 12 After Recloser Setting Mismatch

reference_summary: The triac gate terminal screw had engaged only two threads, creating high resistance in the gate drive path. At 13:20 on 8 September 2026, Synthetic Substation set a new ambient temperature record of 44.2 °C. To satisfy area dispatch, the transformer remained loaded to 128 MVA, which was 13 MVA above its forced-air rating. The earlier cooling-control modification removed the fan current relay, so a start command and actual running status were the same logic point. At 13:38 the controller saw the true oil temperature at 70 °C and issued a start command to fan group B. Because the triac never conducted, the fan motor drew 0 A, yet the panel indicated 'on' because the command voltage existed. The transformer was separated at 14:18; area automatic underfrequency shedding removed 47 MW, and full feeder restoration completed at 15:13. A current transformer was installed in the fan branch; control logic now requires a measured current above 5 A before showing fan on.
title: Triac gate connection failure disables cooling fan group in synthetic substation

reference_summary: Firmware v4.12, installed on 1 July, had an integer underflow that reset fan group B's start setpoint to −273 °C. The triac gate was asserted every half-cycle without an off state, so group B's fans ran continuously since that firmware date. Load dispatcher raised the transformer load to 129 MVA at 14:10, above the rating that requires all fans. At 15:10 the fan motor bearing locked, causing locked-rotor current of 48 amperes. After three seconds, the motor thermal overload relay opened the dedicated 52 breaker to de-energize the fan motor. The transformer was isolated at 15:35, dropping 129 MVA to a group of industrial feeders for the next 46 minutes. Hot-spot temperature was estimated at 126 °C for 26 minutes, which per IEEE model yields 1.2 equivalent hours of lost life. Firmware was rolled back to the previous validated release and a lower saturation limit added in the temperature-setpoint routine. A hard-wired 52 auxiliary contact was connected to the controller; the triac gate is now inhibited when the breaker is open.
title: Firmware underflow causes cooling fan bearing failure in synthetic substation transformer

reference_summary: Auxiliary cable C-S05-07 at Synthetic Substation Five had a torn stress cone from excessive pulling force. The 2021 installation report lists a maximum pull of 9.3 kN, exceeding the specified 6.8 kN limit. At 01:33:02, a partial discharge of 265 pC ignited at the torn stress cone. By 01:33:04, the discharge had formed a carbonized track over the insulation surface. Relay 51-07 channel P indicated 2,025 A; independent channel Q indicated 2,226 A; physical current was 2,150 A. After an inverse-time delay of 28 ms, relay 51-07 issued a trip command to breaker 52-07. The 480 V station-service bus de-energized, dropping the ventilation fan and stopping the battery charger's AC input. The charger's triac, with MT1 and MT2 in the input, commutated off at the next zero crossing because gate pulses stopped. At 01:51, a portable diesel generator was connected to the 480 V bus by a field crew, restoring auxiliary supply. The damaged cable section was cut out and replaced with a new splice using a hydrophobic cold-shrink joint.
title: Synthetic Substation Five Auxiliary Power Loss due to Torn Stress Cone Cable Fault

The as-built drawing listed no concrete slab over the duct bank, so the bucket struck the cable directly. At 14:22:33, the backhoe tooth crushed cable C-M7-22, forming a phase-to-ground arc. The arc's thermal jets vaporized the adjacent cable insulation, creating a three-phase bolted fault after 9 ms. Relay 51-1's channel N measured 2,612 A, while channel M indicated 2,928 A; physical current was 2,740 A. After 45 ms of definite-time delay, relay 51-1 issued a trip command to circuit breaker 52-1. The 480 V auxiliary bus remained deenergized, since neither normal nor generator source supplied it. The battery charger output ceased, and the DC bus decayed from 125.0 V to 118.6 V over 24 minutes. At 14:46:33, an operator manually started the generator and closed breaker 52-2, reenergizing the 480 V bus. The damaged cable section was replaced, and a reinforced concrete duct bank was constructed over the new route.
title: Synthetic Mesa Switching Station Auxiliary Power Loss from Excavation-Induced Cable Strike

reference_summary: At 02:16:40, the restoration controller trusted the cached open position of Synthetic LS-7B instead of reading the closed auxiliary contact. The Synthetic LS-7B status was stuck at 21:36:52 because the manual close report from the field never reached the SCADA system. At 02:15:00, a storm-driven tree limb contacted a conductor on Synthetic Main Feeder 7, producing a 3.2 kA ground fault. At 02:16:51, the controller closed tie switch TS-7/12 because all displayed preconditions, including a false open LS-7B, were satisfied. At 02:17:29, lockout relay 86-T12 latched and kept Synthetic Tie Feeder 12 de-energized until an operator reset it at 03:12. Between 02:16:51 and 02:17:32, the loop controller processed 176 switching commands into its event buffer, saturating the queue. At 03:12, an operator manually reset lockout relay 86-T12 and placed tie switch TS-7/12 in local hold mode. At 03:39, a field crew opened Synthetic LS-7B by local controls, physically isolating the faulted section from the alternate source.
title: Automated Loop Restoration into Unisolated Fault at Synthetic Feeder 7

reference_summary: At 03:14:10, a wind-blown branch struck a conductor on Synthetic North Feeder 22, causing a 4.1 kA phase-to-ground fault. At 03:14:23, phase-overcurrent relay protection sent a trip signal to circuit breaker 52-N22, opening Synthetic North Feeder 22. A damaged gate-driver component left 4.2 V on the gate terminal for 12 ms, delaying block recovery of the phase-A triac. At 03:18:42, the controller considered Synthetic TS-22/23 open after stopping its gate pulses, but phase-A current remained at 310 A. At 03:19:11, lockout relay 86-S23 latched, interrupting Synthetic South Feeder 23 and all restored Synthetic North Feeder 22 load. At 03:20:40, the independent voltage monitor 22/23-VM read 0.4 V between MT1 and MT2, disproving the controller's open-state indication for phase-A. At 03:58, an operator de-energized the triac gate drive and manually verified that MT1-to-MT2 voltage reached 12.0 kV, proving forward blocking. At 04:12, a field crew replaced the defective triac gate-driver board and the damaged MT1-to-MT2 voltage monitor on Synthetic TS-22/23.
title: Solid-State Tie Switch Latch Causes Parallel Restoration Loop at Synthetic North Feeder 22
